calls.head: Ottawa locks it down; Toronto doesn’t
calls.body: Ottawa ranks 2nd of 32 for shot suppression, toward the stingy end; Toronto ranks 32nd, toward the porous end.
calls.call: Ottawa allows fewer 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than Toronto.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts allowed per 60, Ottawa had 69.1 per 60 and Toronto 45.6 per 60. Coming in, Ottawa was at 51.7 per 60 and Toronto at 62.9 per 60.

calls.head: Airtight against leaky on the kill
calls.body: Ottawa ranks 2nd of 32 for penalty kill, toward the airtight end; Toronto ranks 30th, toward the leaky end.
calls.call: Ottawa’s penalty kill allows less per 60 than Toronto’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On expected goals allowed per 60 on the penalty kill, Ottawa had 7.8 per 60 and Toronto 11.8 per 60. Coming in, Ottawa was at 6.8 per 60 and Toronto at 8.3 per 60.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto only a 26% chance, and it went the way we feared.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 74% chance, and Ottawa delivered.

surprises.head: Ottawa got to the dangerous areas
surprises.body: Ottawa needed 8.8 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 15.2 and a league average of 15.9. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 600 games.

surprises.head: Toronto flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Toronto took 60% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Toronto would expect about 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 175 games.
